name: Spondyloepiphyseal Dysplasia with Metatarsal Shortening

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Spondyloepiphyseal Dysplasia with Metatarsal Shortening

criteria.description: Short-trunk dwarfism with disproportionate short stature
Radiographic evidence of metatarsal shortening, especially affecting the first and second metatarsals
Radiological abnormalities of vertebral bodies and epiphyses including platyspondyly and delayed ossification
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Identification of pathogenic variants in COL2A1 gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of disproportionate short-trunk dwarfism with radiographic evidence of metatarsal shortening and vertebral-epiphyseal abnormalities
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for COL2A1 mutations can confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Metatarsal shortening predominantly affecting first and second metatarsals
searchTerms: short toes affecting front foot bones
flattened spine bones with slow bone formation

common.symptomName: Short neck with limited cervical spine mobility

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory restriction due to thoracic cage abnormalities
searchTerms: respiratory problems due to thorax shape

rare.symptomName: Neurological deficits secondary to cervical spine instability
searchTerms: nerve damage from unstable neck bones
neurological symptoms from cervical spine issues
spinal cord problems due to neck instability

rare.symptomName: Cardiovascular anomalies such as mitral valve prolapse

imaging: Radiographs showing platyspondyly and delayed ossification of vertebral bodies
Shortened first and second metatarsals on foot X-rays
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Clinical assessment of disproportionate short-trunk dwarfism

distinguishingFeatures: Earlier onset with more pronounced vertebral and epiphyseal changes
Disproportionate short-limb dwarfism rather than short-trunk
Characteristic facial features including frontal bossing

redFlags: Progressive neurological symptoms indicating cervical spine instability
Severe respiratory compromise due to thoracic cage deformity
Early-onset severe osteoarthritis causing significant disability
references: Superti-Furga A, Unger S. Spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia congenita and related disorders. In: GeneReviews® [Internet]. University of Washington, Seattle; 2020.
